subject: bicycle
pitch: A vintage Dutch city bicycle in mint green. Tall upright handlebars with cream grips and a silver bell, a brown leather saddle with springs, chrome mudguards, a chain guard, a wicker basket on the front filled with sunflowers and a baguette, and whitewall tyres.
reasoning:
Since a bicycle is a prop rather than a creature, I'm thinking the simplest robust approach is to build it from plain three.js meshes placed using the SDK's part function, which takes geometry, color, and positioning via point, joint, frame, and direction parameters.

I'm leaning toward using a dedicated rod or tube helper that connects two points directly, since the exact semantics of aiming a centered geometry along a direction are ambiguous and a two-point connector would be safer for building the bike's frame.

I'll write a helper function that computes the midpoint and direction vector between two points, then places a cylinder part centered there with its length matching the distance, using Vector3 arithmetic rather than any disallowed rotation methods. Since this is a bike rather than a creature, I don't need joints, just a root to attach parts to.

For the basket contents, I'm planning sunflowers made from stem cylinders with flattened disc heads and brown centers, plus a tan capsule-shaped baguette. For the wheels, I'll use torus geometry for the tires with a slightly offset white torus for the whitewall effect, defining wheel radius, wheelbase, and axle positions along the Z-axis so the bike faces forward realistically.

To avoid ambiguity with how direction vectors map to geometry orientation, I've decided to bake all rotations directly into the geometry at build time, then place everything using a simple translation offset — this gives predictable, consistent results rather than relying on uncertain axis-aiming behavior. I'm also working out the vertical placement so the wheels sit correctly on the ground plane.

For creating connecting tubes between two points, I'm writing a helper that computes the midpoint and direction vector, builds a cylinder along that direction, and passes it through the part function using a dir option rather than any forbidden quaternion-alignment methods.

Now I'm settling on a colour palette for the bike scene (mint, cream, chrome, leather brown, black tyres, wicker tan, sunflower yellow, etc) and planning the wheel geometry — torus tyres rotated into the YZ plane with thin whitewall accents positioned slightly off the tube centerline to simulate sidewall stripes.

Working out the rim, hub, and spoke geometry per wheel, then planning mudguards as partial torus arcs rotated and positioned over each wheel's top, computing the arc span and rotation needed to center it correctly.

Now I'm laying out the frame as a diamond structure in the YZ plane, defining key points like the bottom bracket, seat tube top, head tube, and the top/down tube connections to form the bike's main geometry.

I'm continuing with seat stays connecting the seat cluster to the rear hub, chainstays linking the bottom bracket to the rear dropout, and giving the frame tubes a mint green finish. I'm also building the fork legs from the head tube down to the front hub, and planning the handlebar setup with an upright stem and riser leading into swept-back bars.

For the handlebars, I'm placing straight tube segments that rise and sweep backward into left and right arms, with cream grips angled toward the rider, plus small joint spheres at the bends for a cleaner look. I'm also adding a small silver dome-shaped bell mounted on the right side of the handlebar near its mounting bracket.

Then for the seat area, I'm building a seat post rising to the saddle position, with a brown leather box-shaped saddle including a nose extension, and a few stacked thin torus rings underneath to suggest coil springs.

Adding geometry for the chain guard...

Now for pedals, I'll add crank arm tubes running from the bottom bracket down to small pedal boxes at each side, keeping them black and sized so they clear the ground. For the front basket, I'm thinking of a trapezoidal wicker-style box mounted in front of the handlebars near the top of the fork.

For the basket shape itself, I'll use an open-ended tapered cylinder to form a bucket-like body, with a torus rim at the top and a few thinner torus bands stacked down the sides to suggest woven wicker texture, all upright along the Y axis positioned just above and behind the front wheel.

Now I'm working out the basket's placement relative to the frame and wheel so it clears the mudguard, then adding sunflowers inside it -- stems as thin green tubes rising from the basket interior to tilted flower heads, with each head built as a small yellow disc oriented along its stem direction, plus petals.

I'm also sketching the petal rim as a yellow cylinder ring with a brown center disc, keeping things simple rather than modeling individual petals, and planning five sunflowers with optional leaves. Finally, I'm adding a tan baguette as a capsule shape angled diagonally across the basket.

Checking whitewall tube radius against the tyre geometry so it protrudes slightly outward and forms a visible bump band around the tyre surface.

Now working out wheel orientation: rotating the torus by 90° around Y moves its ring plane from XY into YZ, which is what I want for a side-facing wheel. For spokes, I'm planning 16 thin chrome tubes per wheel running radially from the hub center to points around the rim in the YZ plane, giving 32 spoke parts total plus the rims, tyres, and whitewall pieces.

Chrome rims use a torus geometry rotated the same way, colored a metallic grey. I'm structuring the frame construction around a wheel(cz) helper that places rear and front wheels at their respective z-positions, then building chainstays, seat stays, seat tube, and top tube as tubes connecting BB, seat cluster, head tube, and rear hub coordinates so the triangle geometry of the frame holds together properly.

Now I'm defining the fork crown and legs connecting to the front dropouts, then adding the stem, riser, and handlebar arms as segmented tubes with sphere joints at the bends, plus cream-colored grips and a bell clamp positioned on the right side of the bar.

Working out the bell's silver dome shape and placement on the handlebar, then moving to the seat post and saddle — using layered boxes for the main saddle body and nose in brown leather, with spring coils planned to go underneath.

For the chainring, I'm figuring out how to combine a dark cylinder for the ring with a chrome chain guard disc that partially covers it, positioning them so the guard overlaps without completely hiding the ring.

For the chain itself, I'm planning two tube segments (top taut, bottom slack) running from the front ring tangent points to the rear cog, both centered at x=0.

I realize the chain guard, chainring, and chain x-positions don't align, so I'm shifting everything to x≈0.03-0.04 to keep them consistent on the drivetrain side. Then I'm laying out the pedal crank arm and pedal box on the right side only, skipping the left crank for simplicity.

For the wheels, I'm adding chrome hub cylinders rotated to align along the X axis, and dark tires. For the basket, I'm building a conical wicker body using a closed cylinder shape with tapering bands of torus rings stacked at increasing heights, choosing a closed cylinder over an open one so it doesn't look hollow from outside.

I'm now deciding to place the baguette sticking out above the rim with sunflower stems emerging from the top, since the basket geometry itself stays closed and filled items just poke out visually rather than sitting truly inside a hollow cavity.

Working out the basket bands as tori with radius increasing toward the top, and figuring brackets to mount the basket to the frame near the head tube, connecting the rim to a bracket tube positioned to clear the front wheel.

Now I'm building the mudguards as partial tori arcs centered over each wheel, computing the rotation angles so the arc spans symmetrically above the tire with proper clearance, then deriving the endpoint positions for the mudguard stays that connect the mudguard tips down to the fork.

Adding a similar stay for the rear mudguard from the seat cluster to its front edge point. Now I'm placing the wicker basket's color scheme, then working out sunflower positions: stem bases clustered near the basket bottom center, with flower heads offset upward and outward so they fan out above the basket rim.

For each sunflower head, I'm building layered geometry: a yellow petal disc, a tapered petal ring for a star-like silhouette, and a small brown center disc, checking positions so heads don't collide with the handlebars.

I'm skipping leaves for budget, and now placing a baguette inside the basket—a tilted capsule shape positioned diagonally so it peeks out above the rim naturally.

Setting up a helper function to build connecting tubes between two points, computing direction, length, and normalized vectors for the geometry.

Now I'm working out wheel construction, placing the tire torus and whitewall rings, and thinking through how the builder's `at` and `dir` parameters align geometry for consistent positioning.

I'm detailing rim, hub, and spoke placement for the wheel, then extending this to the mudguard shape using a partial-arc torus positioned and rotated to fit over the wheel.

Now I'm defining the frame geometry—plotting key points for the seat, head tube, bottom bracket, and dropouts, then connecting them with tube segments for the top tube, down tube, seat tube, head tube, and chainstays in a mint-colored frame material.

Still placing frame tubes...

Still building fork and stem geometry...

Working out the bell dome placement and bracket connection on the bar, positioning it near the bend point with a small chrome tube linking bar to bell.

For the seat area, I'm building the saddle post with chrome tube, adding spring-ring details using small torus shapes stacked along the seat tube, then constructing the saddle itself from a main box plus a narrower nose box extending forward, keeping the geometry simple rather than attempting curved shell forms.

Now I'm moving to the drivetrain: positioning a chrome chain guard box beside the chainring, sizing and placing it to cover the ring without overlapping the pedal crank arm, then adding the dark chainring cylinder, a tube for the crank arm, and a pedal box sized to align with the crank's bottom end — adjusting the guard's x-position slightly to avoid collision with the crank.

Working out the chain tubes connecting the front ring to the rear hub, deciding to skip drawing a separate rear cog since it would overlap the chrome hub.

Now I'm building the front basket: a tapered wicker wall cylinder, a floor disc, a rim torus at the top, and a series of thin horizontal bands whose radius grows to match the wall's taper, each positioned slightly outside the wall surface.

I'm adding the chrome bracket tube connecting the headtube area up to the basket rim, then moving to a sunflower-building function with a stem tube and a flower head made from a brown disc center surrounded by a ring of yellow frustum-shaped petals oriented along a normal direction.

I'm placing the baguette as a tan capsule tucked diagonally into the basket, checking it won't collide with the sunflower heads above, then double-checking the overall build: both wheels with spokes and mudguards, chrome fork, whitewall tires, leather saddle with springs, chain guard, and bell all accounted for, with everything resting properly above ground level and the total bike height including sunflowers landing around a realistic 1.4-1.45m.

Now I'm setting up the module structure — exporting the metadata, trimming imports down to just what's needed, and defining the flat color palette as hex strings for mint, cream, chrome, leather, wicker, and the other materials. I'm sketching helper functions for tubes, balls, and the wheel construction, starting with the wheel radius constant and beginning the wheel-building logic.

Writing wheel geometry...
